findings.note: The clause hides who should note this. No actor appears in the clause or nearby sentences, and the framing is doing argumentative work that a reader would want attributed.

findings.quote: The decision to sell was made
findings.note: 'Decision' is an action noun carried by 'was made'; the actor who decided is absent.
'Evaluation' is an action noun buried in the empty verb 'carried out'; the verb 'evaluated' exists.

findings.quote: By the time I reached the top of the hill that February,
findings.note: The subject "I" arrives after sixteen words of introductory clause, exceeding the ten-word threshold.

findings.quote: After eleven years of sitting in morning traffic behind a school bus, I
findings.note: The main subject is preceded by 12 words plus a comma. That is 12 words before the subject 'I', counting the introductory phrase.
The word 'picturesque' appears twice within one sentence; the first occurrence is in 'a picturesque row of Victorian houses'.
Doubled pair: 'plain' and 'simple' say the same thing twice.

findings.quote: I reached the bottom of the hill by seven. I arrived at my desk with wet socks and a temper.
findings.note: Three consecutive sentences follow the same 'I + verb + time or place' template, starting at 'I left the house at six-forty.'

findings.quote: My bike was stolen in June.
findings.note: The paragraph is about crossing the Fenwick Road bridge on foot. The sentence introduces a bike theft with no link to the bridge or the crossing.

findings.quote: an anchor that kept me moored
findings.note: Mixed figure: a cocoon and a mooring cannot both hold as images of the same car, and the sentence states the claim twice through incompatible pictures.
Empty figure: what the city opened up to, or what the reader is meant to see in it, is never supplied.

findings.quote: I can only describe what happened to me, in my own circumstances, which may or may not resemble yours.
findings.note: Restatement of the earlier limit 'I am not trying to tell anyone else how to live.'

findings.quote: the top of the hill that February
findings.note: 'the hill' and 'that February' have no antecedent where they stand; both are supplied only in the paragraph beginning 'The first winter was very hard.'
The draft never says who raised the concerns, and the surrounding sentences name no one. The reader cannot tell whether this was the teams, the leads or someone else.
The draft never says who decided that all changes would go through the board process. The actor is a body or role the reader would need in order to judge whether the policy can be changed.
Four consecutive sentences open with the same two words, 'The board'.
The verb 'conduct' carries the noun 'review', burying the action of reviewing.
'Determination' names the act of determining, carried by the empty verb 'makes'.
Doubled pair: 'full and complete' says one thing twice.

findings.quote: a toll booth on the highway to production
findings.note: Stock image standing in for the argument. The draft never establishes what the toll is, who pays it, or why the road is the right picture for a review step.

findings.quote: their median wait from six days to under one
findings.note: The phrase depends on the pilot and both teams, which are not introduced until the paragraph beginning In March and April, the Payments and Search teams ran a pilot. The six-day baseline is explained only in the paragraph beginning Today every production release needs a sign-off from the board.

findings.quote: Flood warnings for Quay Street were not issued
findings.note: The draft never names who was responsible for issuing flood warnings, so no one is accountable for the late warning.
The draft does not say who promised the sandbags, leaving the broken commitment unattributed.
'Decision' buries the verb 'decide' behind the empty verb 'made'.
'Undertaking' is a noun naming the act of undertaking, and the clause's verb is the empty 'given'. The action is buried in the noun rather than carried by the verb.
'Assessment' is a noun naming the act of assessing, and the verb 'carry out' does the work the noun should give to a verb.

findings.quote: At a quarter past four on the ninth of March,
findings.note: The subject 'Ellen Morrow' is preceded by thirteen words of introductory material.

findings.quote: In the weeks after the water went down and the loss adjuster had come round to photograph each and every room,
findings.note: Twenty-three words precede the main subject 'Ellen'.

findings.quote: Gluten development depends on water temperature
findings.note: The previous sentence is about Tom driving for flour; this sentence opens on gluten development and water temperature, an aside the next sentence ('By the end of March she was selling') does not continue from.
sodden appears twice in two sentences; the first is in 'the smell of sodden flour' and the second in 'the sodden skirting boards'.
'Affected' repeats within two sentences; the first occurrence opens the paragraph.
Doubled pair: 'each and every' says one thing twice. The single word 'each' or 'every' would carry the same meaning.

findings.quote: the flood was a wake-up call
findings.note: Stock image standing in for an argument the draft never makes about what the street was meant to change. A wake-up call implies a specific summons and response that the paragraph asserts rather than shows.
A stock image standing in for a claim the draft does not make about the bakery's role on the street.
A cliché that stands in for whatever pressure the council actually came under.

findings.quote: It is difficult to overstate how much the flood affected the people of the street, and it would be impossible to describe every way in which their lives were changed by it.
findings.note: Restatement of 'The flood affected many people on Quay Street in many different ways.' The reader loses no fact.

findings.quote: The insurance payment, when it came in August, covered the ovens
findings.note: This paragraph breaks into the flood-night account begun in 'At a quarter past four on the ninth of March'; the scene resumes at 'She rang her son Tom'. It separates material those two paragraphs hold together.

findings.quote: The flood affected many people on Quay Street
findings.note: This paragraph restates the street-wide impact already asserted in 'It was obviously a shock to the whole street' and adds no new point to it.
The phrase presupposes a specific election that the reader must already know about; no earlier paragraph, and no later one, supplies it.
Seventeen words precede the subject 'a resolution'.

findings.quote: It was decided by the committee
findings.note: Eleven words precede the subject 'a decision'.
'Determination' is an action noun carried by 'made', a weak verb. The action of determining is buried in the noun.
The noun 'decision' buries the verb 'decide', and the clause's only verb is the empty 'made'.
'Expectation' buries the verb 'expect' behind 'There was'. The clause's verb does no work.
'Observation' buries the verb 'observe' behind the empty verb 'made'.
The clause never says who would make the decision. The committee is named in the preceding clause, but the sentence does not state that the committee is the actor here.
The clause hides who conducted the meeting. The reader must infer the chair or committee.

findings.quote: a resolution would be arrived at
findings.note: The draft never says who was expected to arrive at the resolution. The surrounding sentences name no actor for this action.
The draft does not say who failed to arrive at the resolution. No actor appears in the clause or the sentences around it.

findings.quote: It is a feeling that is familiar. It is a feeling that recurs.
findings.note: Two consecutive sentences are built on the identical template 'It is a feeling that...', following 'the feeling that' in the first sentence.
The distinctive word "resolution" recurs in the second sentence, and the construction "arrived at" is repeated as well; the first "resolution" appears in the preceding sentence.
The phrase "was arrived at" repeats from "a resolution would be arrived at" in the previous sentence.

findings.quote: It is a feeling that recurs.
findings.note: The word "feeling" recurs three times in three consecutive sentences. The first occurrence is in "with the feeling that nothing had been accomplished."

findings.quote: It was decided by the committee that a decision would be made regarding the proposal.
findings.note: Repeats the opening paragraph beginning 'It was decided by the committee thxt x determination' and adds no new point.

findings.quote: There was an expectation that a resolution would be arrived at.
findings.note: Repeats the second paragraph beginning 'There was an expectation that' and adds no new point.

findings.quote: Some of us left the room with the feeling that nothing had been accomplished.
findings.note: Repeats the earlier paragraph beginning '*Some of us left the room' and adds no new point.
